content.value_statement: Teams often need different interaction patterns for each Apple platform. This skill provides platform-specific HIG guidance for layouts, navigation, inputs, accessibility, and implementation notes.
actual_capabilities: Identify relevant Apple HIG guidance for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, and games.
Compare platform differences in navigation, input, layout, and conventions.
Recommend adaptation strategies for apps moving across Apple devices.
Provide implementation notes for platform APIs and framework choices when relevant.
Highlight accessibility, comfort, and input considerations from Apple platform references.
limitations: Does not replace testing on real devices or review by Apple.
Reference content can lag behind current Apple documentation.
Does not generate production-ready interface code by itself.
Cannot validate App Store compliance or legal requirements.

use_cases.title: Cross-Platform App Adaptation
use_cases.description: Translate an existing iPhone app into iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS patterns without copying layouts directly.

use_cases.title: Implementation Planning
use_cases.description: Map platform conventions to navigation, input, windowing, and API decisions before building screens.

use_cases.title: Game Interface Review
use_cases.description: Evaluate controls, safe areas, accessibility, and full-screen behavior for games across Apple devices.

prompt_templates.title: Recommend Platform Patterns
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one target platform.
prompt_templates.prompt: I am designing a [type of app] for [Apple platform]. Recommend navigation, input, layout, and accessibility considerations from Apple HIG.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt Across Platforms
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for moving an existing app.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have an existing [base platform] app with [core screens]. Explain how to adapt it for [target platforms] without directly porting the layout.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Platform Differences
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a structured product decision.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [platform A], [platform B], and [platform C] for this workflow: [workflow]. Include input methods, navigation, layout density, system features, and implementation notes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit A Game Experience
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for games across Apple devices.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Apple-platform game concept: [concept]. Assess onboarding, display sizes, controls, full-screen behavior, accessibility, and platform-specific technologies.

output_examples.input: Designing a task manager for iPhone and Mac.
output_examples.output: A concise recommendation separating iOS tab-based navigation and touch targets from macOS menu bar, resizable windows, keyboard shortcuts, and denser layouts.

output_examples.input: Porting a drawing app from iPad to visionOS.
output_examples.output: Guidance explaining when to use windows, volumes, indirect gestures, comfort zones, and minimum immersion for core creative tasks.

output_examples.input: Reviewing a multiplayer game for Apple devices.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering first-play onboarding, aspect ratios, controller alternatives, accessible text, Game Center, haptics, and privacy prompts.

best_practices: Start by naming target platforms, primary device context, and interaction mode.
Ask for platform differences before requesting implementation details or code.
Validate recommendations against current Apple documentation and real-device behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not copy one platform layout directly to every Apple device.
Do not treat this skill as a complete accessibility or App Store review.
Do not use it when the task is unrelated to Apple platform interface design.

faq.question: Which Apple platforms does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, and Apple-platform games.

faq.question: Can it help with SwiftUI or UIKit decisions?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest platform-aware implementation notes, but it does not write or test full code by itself.

faq.question: Does this replace the official Apple HIG?
faq.answer: No. Use it as a guided summary and decision aid, then verify against current Apple documentation.

faq.question: Is it useful for game design?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for controls, onboarding, display sizes, accessibility, and platform technologies for games.

faq.question: Can it compare different Apple platforms?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare navigation, inputs, layout density, system features, and implementation considerations.

faq.question: Does the skill require automatic network access?
faq.answer: No. The skill content is local Markdown with reference links that a user or agent may open separately.
